whenToUse: Screens where people repeatedly open an item from a list and come back.
The list is long and it's easy to lose your place.
whenNotToUse: There are several places to go back to, which are hard to name (leave it to the browser's Back).
The list changes a lot in the meantime (suggest refreshing).
accessibility: Name the back button for where it goes, such as "Back to list".
On return, restore the scroll position and move focus to the item that was opened.
Use it together with the address history so the result matches the browser's Back.
Focus with preventScroll so the screen doesn't jump while restoring the position.
